chunks: Al-Tawhid: Ibn Idris, from his father, from al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn Ismail and Ibn Hashim together, from Safwan, from Ibn Hazim who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does there happen something today which was not in the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? He said: No. Rather it was in His knowledge before He generated the Heavens and the Earth.

key_terms.التَّوْحِيدُ: Divine Unity / The Book of Unity

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about whether new events occur outside of God's knowledge?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Ibn Hazm poses a fundamental question to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding whether any new event occurs that was not previously known to God. The Imam confirms that all things, including future events, were already in God's knowledge before the creation of the heavens and the earth, affirming divine omniscience and pre-eternal knowledge. This hadith is often cited in Shia theological discourse to support the concept of 'Ilm al-Ilahi' (Divine Knowledge) as comprehensive and eternal, distinguishing it from temporal acquisition of knowledge.

en.ammaar-muslim: 8. [8/345] al-Tawhid: Ibn Idris from his father from al-Ash’ari from Ali b. Ismail and Ibn Hashim from Safwan from Ibn Hazim who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام - Does there happen something today which was not in the knowledge of Allah Mighty and Majestic? He said: No. Rather it was in His knowledge before He generated the Heavens and the Earth.
